correctness.rationale: The connected odd graph has unsigned incidence matrix of full row rank: a row-kernel vector must change sign across every edge, so an odd cycle makes it zero. There is one more edge than vertex, and the alternation of signed cycle coefficients ±1 and path coefficients ±2 cancels at every vertex, including both path endpoints. The primitive relation thus gives the principal prime binomial ideal, with degree c+ell. Disjoint monomial supports imply separate gradient ideals; minimal vanishing sets on each side are one squared coordinate or two simple coordinates, yielding exactly the stated incomparable coordinate primes and their parity counts, including ell=1. For the Hilbert calculation, the ideal in s simple variables consisting of monomials with support of size at least s-1 has series s(t/(1-t))^(s-1)+(t/(1-t))^s. Multiplying by the product of the q squared coordinates shifts it by q, with those variables otherwise free; the quotients on the two sides tensor. This proves the numerator and denominator independently of the syzygy assertion. Degree is the count of top-dimensional degree-one components. At the general closed points specified in the assumptions, the binomial factors outside the chosen vanishing coordinates are units, whose square roots exist in the completed local ring in characteristic zero. This gives the stated transverse equations; 'analytic' is interpreted formally over a general field and literally over C, not as a splitting over the possibly non-algebraically closed function field of a generic point. The hypersurface is S2, so a point fails normality exactly when its localization contains a nonregular height-one point, yielding the asserted support. The supplied checker was read, not run. It checks the displayed relation against incidence (rather than deriving it without the proposed weights), exhausts support masks for the named finite samples and does not provide the all-parameter proof.
